sections.heading: Overview

sections.content: To provide to all Transport cluster agencies and their employee’s specific medical and triage assistance post a workplace injury or illness, including psychological injury.
sections.heading: Project goals

sections.content:
· To provide prompt access to triage and if required appropriate medical attention
· A consistent approach with regards to assessing the capacity (not incapacity) of employees and the benefits of early return to work (limiting Lost Time Injuries LTI’s).
· Initial triage of employees where a workers compensation claim may be lodged. The triage should include capture of relevant details; assessment of risk or ‘flags’ and completion of regulator Standard of Practice requirements for self-insured cases.
· Utilisation of doctors with a specific interest in occupational and mental health, and those that understand the NSW Workers Compensation legislation requirements.
· Improved quality assurance systems.
· Central 'free call' or local number as the single point of contact.
· Capacity to accept referrals for medical appointments 24/7/365 and to coordinate medical appointments as required out of hours.
· If the injury or illness is ultimately assessed as work related, costs associated with medical treatment will be billed in accordance with the relevant State Insurance Regulatory Authority (SIRA), or Australian Medical Association (AMA) fee schedule and submitted to the Transport Injury & Health Solutions team or the Transport claims agent in a timely manner. Any case assessed as non-compensable should be covered by the particular Agency, subject to approval by the nominated agency officer.
